Harpreet Singh Brar J. (Oral)
1.

The appellant has approached this Court by filing the present appeal for setting aside the order dated 04.03.2023 passed by the court of Sub Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Sultanpur Lodhi, vide which the respondents No. 1 to 3 have been discharged in a criminal complaint filed under Section Section 420, 465, 467, 468, 471, 474 and 120-B of Indian Penal Code.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. The facts of the case as briefly stated are that the complainant Dr.Kanwarjeet Singh Gill filed the aforesaid complaint against the accused Rakesh Kumar Dhir and others on the allegations that accused Rakesh Kumar Dhir is the President of Managing Committee, accused Vandana Shukla is the Principal and accused Jain Parkash is the Office Superintendent of S.D College for Women,
Sultanpur Lodhi, District Kapurthala and all the accused are hands in glove with each other and have hatched a conspiracy in order to cheat the concerned authorities.

entities.text:
S.D College for Women,
Sultanpur Lodhi
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
The complainant further alleged that accused Vandana Shukla was Principal of S.D College for Women, Sultanpur Lodhi on probation during the year 1 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:146593 2023:PHHC:146593 2006-07 and she submitted her resignation by giving one month's notice on 29.07.2007 and the intimation of her resignation was sent by accused Rakesh Kumar Dhir to the DPI (Colleges) Punjab,
Chandigarh vide letter No.SDC/16863/07 dated 04.08.2007 and that his wife-Harjinder Kaur who was Lecturer in Political Science of the said College was appointed as acting Principal with effect from 30.08.2007 vide order dated 29.08.2007 and she continued to act as Principal of the college Kanwarjeet Singh Gill vs Rakesh Kumar Dhir And Ors on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197186430/
1 upto 22/23.05.2008 and her specimen signatures were sent to various authorities vide letter No.SDC/16894/07 dated 11.09.2007.

entities.text: Kanwarjeet Singh Gill vs Rakesh Kumar Dhir And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thereafter, an advertisement for the post of Principal on regular and permanent basis of S.D College for Women, Sultanpur Lodhi was published in The Tribune, (English as well as Punjabi) on 08.09.2007, 10.01.2008 and 02.04.2008 3.

entities.text: S.D College for Women, Sultanpur Lodhi
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: After being relieved from S.D College for Women, Sultanpur Lodhi, accused Vandana Shukla joined as Principal of Hindu Kanya College, Kapurthala on 30.08.2007 on probation and that before the completion of the probation period, her services were terminated vide letter bearing No.HKCMC/2008 dated 10.04.2008 and one month salary was paid to accused Vandana Shukla in lieu of one month notice period.

entities.text: S.D College for Women, Sultanpur Lodhi
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The complainant further alleged that in pursuance of conspiracy hatched between accused persons, false letters were fabricated and just to extend favour to Vandana Shukla, accused Rakesh Kumar Dhir wrote letter No.SDC/SQR-1, SDC/SQR/Special- 2 dated 10.05.2008 offering job to Vandana Shukla as Principal of the College by ignoring the prescribed procedure for the recruitment of the Principal on permanent and regular basis.

He alleged that the accused Rakesh Kumar Dhir had no legal right to write such letters as there was no employer-employee relation between 2 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:146593 2023:PHHC:146593 Rakesh Kumar Dhir and Vandana Shukla at that time and a false letter No.SDC/SPL4 dated 27.05.2008 was written by Rakesh Kumar Dhir misleading that Vandana Shukla was on leave and had joined on 23.05.2008 and on the basis of this false and misleading letter, approval of DPI(C) Punjab was accorded and that the letters dated 10.05.2008 and 27.05.2008 issued by Rakesh Kumar Dhir were self-contradictory and false numbers were appended on the same in connivance with accused Jain Parkash, Office Superintendent of the said College just to extend favour to accused Vandana Shukla.

He further alleged that the approval from DPI Punjab,
Chandigarh was obtained by misleading as while obtaining approval, true facts regarding previous resignation by accused Vandana Shukla, were concealed and false facts regarding accused Vandana Shukla being on leave were put forth with concerned authorities.

He sought copies of above-said letters and their reference numbers but the accused in connivance with each other, had been managing to furnish evasive reply, which forced him to move to the State Information Commissioner for obtaining the same.

The complainant further alleged that he demanded the copy of the documents on the basis of which accused Vandana Shukla joined as the Principal of SD College for Women, Sultanpur Lodhi but the same was not supplied rather Vandana Shukla wrote a letter to his wife Harjinder Kaur stating the information sought by her husband is of confidential nature and supplying of same is not in the larger public interest and she threatened his wife Harjinder Kaur.

entities.text: SD College for Women, Sultanpur Lodhi
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: He further alleged that the accused persons, despite order of the State Information Commissioner, did not supply the sought documents and he was compelled to file CWP No.14864 of 2010 before Hon'ble Punjab & Haryana High Court and Hon'ble High Court vide order dated 26.11.2010 3 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:146593 2023:PHHC:146593 directed that the complete file be submitted and in consequence thereof the documents were received and many of them were found to be false and fabricated and that the approval was accorded regarding joining of accused Vandana Shukla by DPI(C) Punjab, Chandigarh on the basis of letter No.SDC/SPL-4 dated 27.05.2008 written by accused Rakesh Kumar Dhir, President, SD College for Women but the college denied the existence of said letter when the supply of this letter was sought under Right to Information Act, 2005.

Vide letter No.SDC/18032/11 dated 21.11.2011, it was stated that there is no letter No.SDC/SPL-4 dated 27.05.2008 available in the record of the college and that accused Kanwarjeet Singh Gill vs Rakesh Kumar Dhir And Ors on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197186430/
2

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Rakesh Kumar Dhir in connivance with accused Vandana Shukla and Jain Parkash wrote another false letter No.SDC/17120/08 dated 09.06.2008 which was addressed to the Registrar, Guru Nanak Dev university, Amritsar, for getting approval of joining (23.05.2008) of accused Vandana Shukla as Principal of S D College for Women, Sultanpur Lodhi.

entities.text: S D College for Women, Sultanpur Lodhi
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The complainant further alleged that he filed complaints to various public authorities including SSP Kapurthala, Principal Secretary Higher Eduction, Punjab but no action has been taken against the accused and an inquiry was conducted by Department of Education and Mrs. Harleen Bedi, Assistant Director, Intec, in her report dated 08.02.2013, pointed out illegality in clear and categorical terms but again no action has been taken so far.
Hence the present complaint.

4. Learned counsel for the appellant contends that learned Sub Divisional Judicial Magistrate,
Sultanpur Lodhi summoned the respondents No. 1 to 3 vide its order dated 06.08.2016 in complaint No. COMI/44/2014 dated 20.08.2014.

entities.text:
Sub Divisional Judicial Magistrate,
Sultanpur Lodhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Thereafter, respondents No. 1 to 3 filed Criminal Revision Petition No. 243 dated 28.11.2016, challenging the 4 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:146593 2023:PHHC:146593 summoning order.

Learned Additional Sessions Judge, Kapurthala, vide its order dated 21.09.2018 dismissed the Revision Petition filed by respondents No. 1 to 3 and upheld the summoning order dated 06.08.2016 passed by learned SDJM, Sultanpur Lodhi and respondents were directed to appear before the learned trial Court on 05.10.2018.
5. Learned counsel for the appellant contends that learned SDJM, Sultanpur Lodhi has committed serious illegality and material irregularity in discharging the respondents in a very perverse manner.

6. Having heard learned counsel for the petitioner and perusing the record, it transpires that the appellant has filed the complaint under Sections 420, 465, 467, 468, 471, 474 and 120-B of Indian Penal Code against respondents No. 1 to 3 and the learned trial Court after taking cognizance of the said complaint summoned the respondents No. 1 to 3 vide summoning order dated 06.08.2016 by issuing process under Section 204 of Code of Criminal Procedure for the offences provided under Section 420 read with Section 120-B of Indian Penal Code.

Once the summoning order dated 06.08.2016 was upheld by learned Additional Sessions Judge, Kapurthala vide order dated 21.09.2018, learned trial Court should not have discharged the respondents No. 1 to 3.
The issue involved in the present case is well settled by a three Judges Bench of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Adalat Prasad Vs. Rooplal Jindal 2004 RCR (Criminal) 1.

entities.text: Adalat Prasad Vs. Rooplal Jindal 2004 RCR (Criminal) 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relevant paragraph of the said judgment is reproduced hereinbelow:
"15.

It is true that if a Magistrate takes cognizance of an offence, issues process without there being any allegation against the accused or any material implicating the accused or 5 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:146593 2023:PHHC:146593 in contravention of provision of Sections 200 and 202, the order of the Magistrate may be vitiated, but then the relief an aggrieved accused can obtain at that stage is not by invoking Section 203 of the Code because the Criminal Procedure Code does not contemplate a review of an order.

Hence in the absence of any review power or inherent power with the subordinate criminal courts, the remedy lies in invoking Section 482 of Code."

3 7.

entities.text: Kanwarjeet Singh Gill vs Rakesh Kumar Dhir And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The ratio of law as culled out by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Adalat Prasad (supra) was reiterated by a three Judges Bench of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Subramanium Sethuraman Vs. State of Maharashtra and Another 2004 AIR (Supreme Court) 4711.
8.

entities.text: Subramanium Sethuraman Vs. State of Maharashtra and Another 2004 AIR (Supreme Court) 4711
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It has been categorically held that once the summoning order is issued by the Magistrate, even if the order is erroneous, the Magistrate has no power to discharge the accused as it would amount to review and recalling of the summoning order.
The remedy lies against the summoning order is under Section 482 of Cr.P.C.
The learned trial Court has discharged the respondents No. 1 to 3 at the time of framing of charges which is against the settled principle of law.
Therefore, in the opinion of this Court, the impugned order is not sustainable in the eyes of law.
In view of the settled law, the case is decided in limine only with a view to save the process of Court and to curtail the litigation cost of respondents No. 1 to 3.

The impugned order dated 04.03.2023 passed by Sub Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Sultanpur Lodhi in COMI-44/2014 titled as Dr. Kanwarjeet Singh Gill Vs.
Rakesh Kumar Dhir etc. is hereby set aside.

entities.label: COURT

Rakesh Kumar Dhir etc
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The case is remanded back to the learned Sub Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Sultanpur Lodhi to proceed with the case strictly in 6 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:146593 2023:PHHC:146593 accordance with law.

entities.text: Sub Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Sultanpur Lodhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 9. However, the respondents No. 1 to 3 would be at liberty to challenge the summoning order by invoking appropriate remedy before the appropriate forum in accordance with law.
10. In view of the facts and circumstances of the present case, this Court finds merit in the present appeal and the leave to appeal is granted.
Resultantly, the main appeal is also allowed.

(HARPREET SINGH BRAR)
17.11.2023 JUDGE Ajay Goswami
